ai.description: The Kannan caecilian reaches 20–25 cm. It is dark brown to purplish-grey with a pale venter. Key features include a distinct tail, visible primary annuli, and a terminal shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus narayani* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct terminal shield, as its tail tip is rounded and lacks the hardened, flattened skin found in others.
ai.habitat: The Kannan Caecilian inhabits moist, leaf-littered soil within evergreen forests and cardamom plantations in the Western Ghats at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kannan Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows to forage for earthworms and small invertebrates in moist soil after rainfall.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uraeotyphlus narayani* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 10–20 eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kannan Caecilian is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations between 300 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kannan Caecilian produces a faint, high-pitched, rhythmic clicking sound, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in its humid forest habitat.
